scenario: [LOPQ.2.3]: an opaque type is its declaration. `a` and `b` each declare an opaque `Key`, and a rule compares a slot of each. A compiler comparing bare names sees one type and compiles it. PATH PINNED: `dsc.imports.limp_1_5_decl`, which stamps each `Key` with the library declaring it, then `dsc.typecheck`'s comparison of the two `lk_opaque` leaves.
rules_ds:
import a
import b

rule r:
    a.Ba x
    b.Bb y where x.token == y.token
->
    log info "x"

libraries.a:
opaque type Key over Bytes

schema Ba scope logical:
    k: Int key
    token: Key mutable
libraries.b:
opaque type Key over Bytes

schema Bb scope logical:
    k: Int key
    token: Key mutable
